questions.question: ______ is the process of turning on a computer and powering up the system.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Booting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Booting is the process of turning on a computer and powering up the system**__. 

 __
 
• In other words, it is a startup sequence that starts the operating system of a computer when it is turned on.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **There are two types of Booting-**

 
 
• **Warm Booting**

 
 
• It is the process of restarting a computer.
 
• Warm boots are typically initiated by a "Restart" command in the operating system.
 
 
 
• **Cold Booting**
 
 
• It is the process of starting a computer from shutdown or a powerless state and setting it to normal working condition.
 
• It refers to the general process of starting the hardware components of a computer, laptop, or server to the point that its operating system and all startup applications and services are launched.

questions.question: ______ plains are formed due to the weathering of soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karst**__.

__
 
• **Karst plains are formed due to the weathering of soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Karst **is a distinctive topography in which the landscape is largely shaped by the dissolving action of water on **carbonate bedrock** such as **limestone and dolomite**, etc.

 
 
• When the rain falls through the atmosphere, it picks carbon dioxide which dissolves in the droplets.
 
• Once the rain hits the ground, it percolates through the soil and picks more carbon dioxide to form a weak solution of carbonic acid.
 
• The infiltrating water naturally exploits cracks in the rock.
 
• Over long periods, carbon bedrock begins to dissolve.
 
• Opening in bedrock increases in size and an underground drainage system begins to develop and allows more water to pass which further accelerates the formation process of karst.
 
• **Some of the landforms develop within the bedrock such as pools, sinkholes, doline, stalactites, stalagmites etc.**
 
• **​​Examples of karst topography:**
 
 
• Skocjan Caves, Slovenia
 
• The Puerto Princesa Underground River, Philippines
 
• Doline in the causse de Sauveterre, Lozere, France
 
• Li River, Guilin, China

questions.question: What happens to Indian exports when Indian rupee is devalued?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exports become cheaper**__.

__
 
• **Exports become cheaper when the Indian rupee is devalued**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Devaluation occurs when a country intentionally reduces the value of its currency relative to one or more foreign countries**.

 
 
• When the country follows a fixed exchange rate regime the government constantly has to revalue and devalue the currency to maintain the pegged exchange rate.
 
• When there is upwards market pressure on the currency to appreciate, the central bank will artificially devalue the currency by buying up foreign reserves.
 
• Devaluation occurs when a government wishes to increase its balance of trade by decreasing the relative value of its currency.
 
 
 
• Since the value of Indian currency decreases,** it makes Indian goods cheaper which in turn encourages foreign countries to import more goods** from India.
 
• The foreign countries find it extremely profitable to import goods from India when the INR is devalued, hence, exports become cheaper too.
 
• In the short term, a devaluation tends to cause inflation, higher growth and increased demand for exports.

questions.question: Which part of soil has organic materials incorporated with the mineral matter, nutrients and water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Horizon A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Horizon A part of soil has organic materials incorporated with the mineral matter, nutrients and water**__.
 
• Soil horizons are layers parallel to the soil surface whose physical, chemical and biological characteristics differ from the layers above and beneath.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• There are commonly 5 layers or horizons found in the soil. **They are known as O, A, B, C & R horizons.**

 
 
• O Horizon Soi:l It contains a huge amount of organic matter.
 
• A Horizon Soil: It is a leached mineral horizon (dark in color) with a high content of organic matter. This horizon is also called ‘Topsoil’.
 
• B Horizon Soil: This horizon is a zone of accumulation of fine materials and mineral Precipitates like clay, iron, carbonates, gypsum, etc. This horizon is also called ‘Subsoil’.
 
• C Horizon Soil: This horizon contains rock fragments of different sizes (partly weathered rocks).
 
• R Horizon Soil: This layer is composed of hard bedrock (unaltered rock layer).

questions.question: ______ are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep sea plains**__.

__
 
• **Deep-sea plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Ocean Floor Division can be divided into various parts such as Continental Shelf, Continental Slope, Continental Rise or Foot, Deep Ocean basins, Abyssal plains or Deep Sea plain, Oceanic Trenches, Seamounts, and Guyots.
 
 
• **Deep-Sea Plain or Abyssal plain**

 
 
• These plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins.
 
• These are the flattest and smoothest regions of the world.
 
• It is an underwater plain on the deep ocean floor, usually found at depths between 3,000 and 6,000m.
 
• These plains are covered with fine-grained sediments like clay and silt.
 
• Lying generally between the foot of a continental rise and a mid-ocean ridge, abyssal plains cover more than 50% of the Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Deeps or Trenches**
 
 
• These areas are the deepest parts of the oceans.
 
• The trenches are relatively steep-sided, narrow basins.
 
• They are some 3-5 km deeper than the surrounding ocean floor.
 
• They occur at the bases of continental slopes and along island arcs and are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Continental Shelf**
 
 
• The continental shelf is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
 
• It is the shallowest part of the ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less.
 
• The shelf typically ends at a very steep slope, called the shelf break.
 
 
 
• **Continental Slope**
 
 
• The continental slope connects the continental shelf and the ocean basins.
 
• It begins where the bottom of the continental shelf sharply drops off into a steep slope.
 
• The gradient of the slope region varies between 2-5°.
 
• The depth of the slope region varies between 200 and 3,000 m.
 
• The slope boundary indicates the end of the continents.

questions.question: Identify the Indian state which was known as 'Pragjyotisha' during the epic period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• In ancient Sanskrit literature, both the names** ‘Pragjyotisha’ and ‘Kamrupa’ **were used as a designation for ancient Assam.

 
 
• Its antiquity can be established from the fact that it has been mentioned in the two great epics- The Mahabharata and the Ramayana and also in the Puranas.
 
• Regarding the name ‘Prajyotisha’ or ‘Pragjyotishpura’, Gait (1992, reprint) writes that **Prag means ‘former’ or ‘eastern’ and Jyotisha ‘a star’, astrology, shining.** Pragjyotishpur may, therefore, be taken to mean the ‘City of Eastern Astrology’.
 
 
 
• References of Kamarupa are found in literature as well as in many epigraphs.
 
 
• The mythology regarding the origin of the name Kamarupa tells us the story of Sati who died due to the discourtesy shown to her husband by her father Daksha.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is the SI unit for measuring pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pascal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pascal is the SI unit for measuring pressure**__.

 __
 
• The unit is named after Blaise Pascal, a French mathematician and physicist.
 
• 1 Pascal is equal to 1 Newton per Meter squared.
 
• In base units, 1 Pascal is equivalent to 1 kg⋅m−¹⋅s−².
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Candela** is the SI unit of luminous intensity.

 
 
• Luminous intensity is the quantity of visible light that is emitted in unit time per unit solid angle.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin** is the SI unit of temperature.
 
• **Ampere** is the SI unit of electric current.

questions.question: Kabartal Wetland was designated as a Ramsar site in 2020. In which of the following states is it located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

__
 
• **Kabartal Wetland in Bihar was designated as a Ramsar site in 2020**__. 

 __
 
• The Site is one of 18 wetlands within an extensive floodplain complex.
 
• This absorption of floodwaters is a vital service in Bihar State where** 70% of the land is vulnerable to inundation.**
 
• During the dry season, areas of marshland dry out and are used for agriculture.
 
• Significant biodiversity is present, with 165 plant species and 394 animal species recorded, including 221 bird species.
 
• The Wetland is an important stopover along the Central Asian Flyway, with 58 migratory waterbirds using it to rest and refuel.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramsar Convention on Wetlands is an international treaty for “the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands”.**

 
 
• It is also known as the Convention on Wetlands and is named after the city of Ramsar in Iran.
 
• The treaty was established in 1971 by UNESCO and came to force in 1975.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Telangana become the 29th state of India after the reorganisation of the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Telangana became the 29th state of India after the reorganisation of the state of Andhra Pradesh in 2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Telangana became the 29th state of India in 2014 by reorganizing Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
• Lok Sabha passed the Telangana bill on 18th February 2014.
 
• Rajya Sabha passed the Telangana bill on 20th February 2014.
 
• Telangana bill received the President's assent on 1st March 2014.
 
• Telangana was formed as the 29th state of India on 2nd June 2014.
 
 
 
• **Srikrishna Committee **was set up by the center to look into the need for a separate state of Telangana from Andhra Pradesh, and which had accorded the highest priority to a non-separation of the state. The committee was headed by former chief justice B. N. Srikrishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Four icons of Telangana are:**

 
 
• State Bird - Palapitta (Indian Roller or Blue Jay)
 
• State Animal - Jinka (Deer)
 
• State Tree - Jammi Chettu (Prosopis Cineraria)
 
• State Flower - Tangedu (Tanner’s Cassia)

questions.question: In which of the following states did the Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 2020 come into force in December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

__
 
• **The Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 2020 come into force in Gujarat in December 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **The State Government of Gujarat had been witnessing increasing land grabbing activities in the state for the past few years.**

 
 
• Under the law, anyone who illegally grabs land provides money for construction, threatens the owner, extorts rent, or helps in any such activity will be considered a land grabber.
 
• Section 3, read along with Section 4, deems land grabbing prohibited and unlawful in all forms. Any activity arising out of or connected with the same shall be a punishable offense under the legislation.
 
• Any person who continues to engage in this occupation shall be guilty of the wrongdoing of land grabbing.
 
• Actions in violation of these provisions shall invite imprisonment for not less than ten years. This period of punishment may extend up to fourteen years.
